 Research Assistant

 London School of Economics and Political Science 

 - Programme on Innovation and Diffusion (POID) at LSE 

 Location: 

 London

 37,244 to £42,397 per annum inclusive with potential to progress to £45,358 pa inclusive of London allowance

 Hours: 
 Full Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 12th November 2026 

 Closes: 
 29th November 2026 

 LSE is committed to building a diverse, equitable and truly inclusive university   

 Salary from £37,244 to £42,397 per annum  inclusive with potential to progress to £45,358 pa inclusive of London allowance 

 Funding is available to support this position for 1 year with option to renew for 2 years. 

 The Programme on Innovation and Diffusion ( POID ) is seeking to appoint a Research Assistant for a one-year period. The project will use cutting-edge research into how to boost productivity through nurturing innovation – ideas that are new to the world – and how to diffuse these ideas across the economy.

 The project is led by Professor John Van Reenen. The role-holder will play a major role in the planning, design, and implementation of the project and will co-author all outputs accordingly. The role will assist with data matching, processing, modelling, and analysis and will contribute to co-authored top-journal-quality publications.

 The successful candidate should have an undergraduate degree in Economics or other quantitative discipline. A Masters in Economics or other quantitative sciencediscipline (but must have very good knowledge of Economics) by post start date is desirable.

 Essential criteria include: Advanced experience of using Stata for analysing large scale micro data sets; Experience of large-scale data driven projects; Experience of data work requiring great accuracy and attention to detail; Ability to identify appropriate methods of economic investigation; Ability to interpret and analyse patterns or trends in data; and Ability to think through economic problems analytically. Ability to perform literature reviews for obtaining data from data providers and running surveys; Excellent written and verbal communication skills and Ability to convey technical material in non-technical terms for policy and other non- academic stakeholders are essential, as is the collation, presentation of other team members’ work and integration of this into own work as required . The ability to work independently for long time periods without close supervision is also a requirement. A demonstrated knowledge of and interest in economics of innovation and technological change, the wider context of industrial/growth strategy and current policy issues related to productivity is desirable. 

 Visit https://poid.lse.ac.uk/ for information about POID, and https://cep.lse.ac.uk/ for information about POID’s related Centre for Economic Performance

 We offer an occupational pension scheme, generous annual leave and excellent training and development opportunities.

 For further information about the post, please see the how to apply document , job description and the person specification. 

 Applications must take the form of a full Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume, a Covering Letter and an electronic copy of one relevant research paper

 If you have any technical queries with applying on the online system, please use the “contact us” links at the bottom of the LSE Jobs page. Should you have any queries about the role, please email C.H.Tocock@lse.ac.uk

 The closing date for receipt of applications is Sunday 29 November 2026 (23.59 UK time). 

 Regrettably, we are unable to accept any late applications. 

 Any offer of employment is subject to the successful candidate having the right to work in the UK.

 Skilled Worker visa sponsorship may be considered for this role.

 About us 

 The UCL Faculty of Engineering Sciences brings together ten academic departments undertaking world-leading research and teaching across a broad range of engineering disciplines. At UCL Mechanical Engineering, we develop innovative solutions to some of society’s most pressing challenges, from low-carbon shipping to sustainable propulsion systems and fuels.

 This post forms part of a major industry-sponsored collaboration between UCL, bp, the University of Leeds, Imperial College London and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign focused on supporting the transition to sustainable aviation fuels (SAF). As SAF adoption increases, understanding how bio-feedstocks affect material corrosion is critical to ensuring the long-term integrity of refinery infrastructure and components. The project will develop advanced modelling tools to predict corrosion and material degradation, supporting the deployment of digital corrosion-management solutions.

 About the role 

 We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the Applied Metallics Group and contribute to a large-scale collaborative programme investigating bio-feedstock-induced corrosion. Working closely with researchers across academia and industry, you will develop physics-based and physics-informed machine learning models to predict corrosion across a range of materials and processing environments.

 Key responsibilities include assessing and advancing thermodynamic, continuum and atomistic modelling approaches; developing predictive models for corrosion behaviour and material degradation; creating physics-informed machine learning frameworks trained on experimental data; and using these tools to identify material descriptors relevant to corrosion performance. The postholder will work closely with industrial and academic partners, disseminate findings, and contribute to high-quality scientific publications.

 About you 

 You will hold a PhD, or possess equivalent research experience, in a relevant discipline such as materials science, mechanical engineering, computational engineering or a related field. You will have strong expertise in machine learning applied to materials design, optimisation or degradation studies, alongside demonstrable experience of multiscale modelling approaches, including atomistic modelling or related computational techniques.

 The successful candidate will have a proven ability to develop and deliver independent research programmes addressing complex materials challenges, supported by a strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals. Experience applying multiple computational approaches to materials research is essential, as is the ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams. You will also have experience collaborating with industry and experimental researchers, reflecting the highly collaborative nature of this project.

 Further information 

 This Grade 7 position is available for 22 months and is primarily based onsite at UCL’s Bloomsbury campus. The post is funded at Spine Point 32 (£47,186 per annum, inclusive of London Weighting).

 Applicants should submit a CV and supporting statement addressing each criterion in the Job Description and Person Specification, as applications will be assessed against these requirements.

 Equality, Diversity and Inclusion 

 As London’s Global University, UCL recognises that diversity of thought, background and experience strengthens research, teaching and innovation. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and particularly welcome applications from groups currently underrepresented within our workforce.

 UCL Mechanical Engineering holds an Athena Swan Bronze Award in recognition of its commitment to advancing gender equality and fostering an inclusive culture for staff and students.

 Job description 

 Full-time, Fixed-term Contract (36 months) 

 Closing date for applications: 23:59 on 7 th Dec 2026 

 Interviews will be held : 17 th Dec 2026 (Shortlisted candidates may be asked to give a brief research presentation) 

 By reference to applicable SOC code for this role, sponsorship may be possible under Skilled Worker Route. Applicants wishing to consider SWR must ensure that they are able to meet the points requirement before applying. There is further information about this on UK Visas and Immigration Website UK Visas and Immigration Website .

 How can intelligence emerge when a brain and body interact, rather than being designed separately? 

 A new Leverhulme Trust-funded project at the University of Reading, led by Dr Yoshikatsu Hayashi, will explore how intelligence could emerge from interactions between soft materials, a robotic body and its environment. Engineers usually design a robot’s controller and body separately, then connect them, i.e., brain controls body. Living organisms develop from a single cell. As an animal grows, without 'watch maker', its nervous system and body continually influence each other to adapt to changing environments. Body movement generates sensory feedback, which shapes the neural networks controlling future actions. Through this ongoing signalling, behaviours such as crawling, walking, and a goal-oriented behaviour can emerge. 

 Neural communication fundamentally relies on the movement of charged particles called ions. Interestingly, ions also flow through water-rich hydrogels, where polymer networks can guide their movement. Could this provide a primitive form of electrical communication without neurons? Previous research demonstrated that electroactive gels could improve their performance in the computer game Pong through feedback, suggesting that soft matter can exhibit adaptive behaviour without living neurons. 

 By exploring how brain-like control and body movement might emerge together from physical matter, the research aims to uncover fundamental principles of Physical AI and inspire future generations of intelligent soft robots. 

 Curious about the science? Read about the fascinating 'Gel Brain' research in Nature:  https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-02704-y 

 Working with Dr Yoshikatsu Hayashi, you will develop and characterise electroactive hydrogel systems, integrate them with soft robotic platforms and sensorimotor feedback, and investigate the emergence of gait and goal-directed learning. The role provides opportunities for interdisciplinary research, computational modelling, international collaboration and high-quality publications. 

 You will have: 

 A PhD (awarded or near completion) in physics, engineering, soft matter, materials science, or a closely related field. 

 Research experience in at least one of nonlinear dynamics, electroactive/active soft matter, soft robotics, or machine learning. 

 Strong communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively across disciplines. 

 Experience with soft matter physics, hydrogels, multi-electrode measurements, embedded control, reinforcement learning or reservoir computing is desirable, but not all are required. 

 Informal contact details 

 Contact Name: Dr Yoshikatsu Hayashi 

 Contact Job Title: Associate Professor 

 Contact Email address: y.hayashi@reading.ac.uk 

 We welcome applications from both external and internal candidates. As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role can be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Internal candidates should discuss this with their line manager prior to applying. 

 The University is committed to having a diverse and inclusive workforce, supports the gender equality Athena SWAN Charter and the Race Equality Charter, and champions LGBT+ equality. We are a Disability Confident Employer (Level 2). Applications for job-share, part-time and flexible working arrangements are welcomed and will be considered in line with business needs.

 Research Assistant

 Queen Mary University of London 

 - School of Economics and Finance 

 Location: 

 London

 Salary: 

 £39,187 to £39,802
 per annum pro rata

 Hours: 
 Part Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 12th November 2026 

 Closes: 
 26th November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 11028 

 About the Role 

 The Research Assistant will support a research project led by Dr Sam Altmann in Econometrics, with a focus on empirical industrial organisation and structural econometrics.

 The project investigates the empirical content of models of storable goods, such as laundry detergent, in the spirit of Hendel and Nevo’s 2006 paper in Econometrica. The research aims to understand what can be learned about the demand for these types of goods from just standard panel data on household purchases. 

 A key component of the project is the replication of the estimator used in Hendel and Nevo 2006, as well as a simulation study to validate their estimator.

 About You 

 The Research Assistant will play a central role in running a simulation study of Hendel and Nevo’s estimator. In collaboration with and under the supervision of Dr Altmann, this will involve coding up a version of their estimation method, as well as writing code to allow the simulation of data from their model.

 The role predominantly involves the coding of dynamic demand models, as well as Generalised Method of Moments estimators. Prior experience of both aspects is not necessary, but some familiarity or experience of coding dynamic choice problems (such as Bellman or Policy Iteration) and/or experience of coding maximum likelihood or method of moments estimators (such as multinomial logit) is required.

 The position requires a high level of attention to detail, experience of statistical programming, and the ability to follow and refine systematic coding procedures. The Research Assistant will also contribute to ensuring the reliability and reproducibility of the simultation study through careful documentation and validation.

 About the School 

 The School of Economics and Finance is a leader in teaching and research at both the national and international level. It has a range of both undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including programmes that are jointly run with other Schools. The School has over 1000 undergraduate students, and over 500 postgraduate taught students. It offers excellent facilities and resources to enhance learning, including offering training and access to real time trading software to both UG and PGT students.    

 About Queen Mary 

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

 Benefits 

We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated games researcher to join our multidisciplinary team of researchers. The successful applicant will be affiliated with the Sir Peter Rigby Digital Futures Institute and work on computer games, digital twins, gamification and simulation systems. Flexible hybrid and remote working arrangements are supported.

The researcher will take independent responsibility for a range of simulation and visualisation projects involving the development of computer games, digital twins in smart cities, gamification for rehabilitation and Virtual and Augmented Reality systems to simulate climate change. By programming in a game engine, they will contribute to the methodological and scientific delivery of the research, ensuring high standards of data quality and research governance, and play an active role in hands-on games projects, data analysis, academic publications and dissemination. The role will also involve contributing to research funding applications, supporting the supervision of postgraduate students and collaborating with researchers, clinical partners and industry partners across the UK and Europe.

We welcome applications from candidates with a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Games, Software Engineering, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline, alongside relevant research experience in games. A PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline would be advantageous. Previous research publication experience is essential, with a strong record of publications relevant to games research being particularly advantageous.

The post is funded by SPR-DFI for 8 months, subject to continued funding and successful progression beyond the trial period.

The anticipated start date for this role is early January 2027; however, a start date in early February 2027 may be considered.

 About The Role 

 Graduate Research Assistant/Postdoctoral Research Associate in Evidence Synthesis and Medical Statistics 

 This full time post is available from January 2027 on a full time basis until 31st March 2028.

 This post is offered as a fixed term contract and is funded by NIHR (National Institute for Health and Care Research) until 31st March 2028. 

 In line with the University’s fair employment for all principles ,  any further funding opportunities identified will be reviewed and discussed during the contract. 

 The GRA starting salary will be from £34,360, with the PDRA starting salary from £35,302 on Grade E, depending on knowledge, skills and experience.

We welcome applications from candidates interested in working part-time hours or job-sharing arrangements.

 The  Role 

 The Faculty of Health and Life Sciences wishes to recruit either a Graduate Research Assistant or Postdoctoral Research Associate to support the work of a small focussed team who conduct responsive, high-quality systematic reviews to support pressing public health and health service priority issues. The successful applicant will join Isca Evidence, a multidisciplinary team of systematic reviewers, epidemiologists, statisticians, health economists, information specialists, clinical experts and members of the public, in producing responsive, high-quality outputs under strict deadlines.

As part of this post, you will contribute to the delivery and ongoing maintenance of a living network meta-analysis.

 About You 

 The successful applicant will be able to present information on research progress and outcomes, communicate complex information, orally, in writing and electronically and prepare proposals and applications to external bodies.

For the GRA role, you will be a graduate trainee with a relevant degree in a field related to health services research for example medical sciences, statistics, or economics, and a demonstrated career commitment to working in health services research.

 For the PDRA Role, you will possess a PhD in a field related to health services research for example medical sciences, statistics, or economics, and a demonstrated career commitment to working in health services research.

Working within Isca Evidence you will support evidence synthesis projects for the Department of Health and Social Care. Supported by experienced team members, you will develop a profile as an emerging expert in evidence synthesis to inform decision making. This will include undertaking suitable training, a personal development plan and identification of opportunities for ongoing learning. As part of the general expectations of this post, you will support publications in high quality international journals and participate in all aspects of the evidence review process.

 Please ensure you read the Job Description and Person Specification for full details of this role.  

 Further information 

 Please contact Jo Thompson Coon, e-mail j.thompson-coon@exeter.ac.uk or G.J. Melendez-Torres, email g.j.melendez-torres@exeter.ac.uk .

 How we can help 

 If you are considering applying and need support to do so, please get in touch with us at hrhelpdesk@exeter.ac.uk . You can request reasonable adjustments within your application or by contacting us. You can also choose to be considered under our Disability Confident Scheme and find out here how this is managed during our recruitment and onboarding process.

Part time Post-Doctoral Research Assistant - Sustainable Fashion and Behaviour Change (Fixed Term)
What helps people repair, reuse and care for their clothes, and what gets in the way? Join Bath Spa University’s Future Fashion Works to research how community hubs can make sustainable fashion more accessible through Restitch the Future, a four-year programme delivered with A Single Thread CIC and supported by The National Lottery Community Fund’s Climate Action Fund.
 
This is a part time role, with a working pattern of 22.2 hours per week (0.6 FTE).

About the Role
Develop and deliver a focused research and evaluation programme with Future Fashion Works, A Single Thread CIC and participating community hubs.
Design and carry out research into clothing consumption, repair and reuse, using appropriate qualitative, quantitative and participatory methods.
Establish baselines and track change across selected hubs, exploring what supports lasting behaviour change and how to reach people who have not previously taken part.
Investigate barriers to participation and work with the project’s EDI Advisory Board and delivery partners to make research and feedback accessible to underrepresented communities.
Develop practical research tools, support hub partners with data collection and analyse the findings. Secure ethical approvals and follow University requirements for consent, safeguarding and data protection.
Use the findings to inform the national community engagement strategy and practical playbook for sustainable fashion hubs. Contribute evidence to funder reports and produce peer-reviewed publications, conference contributions and accessible outputs for practitioners and communities.
About You
A completed PhD or equivalent doctoral-level research experience in a relevant discipline, with evidence of high-quality research outputs appropriate to career stage.
Experience of designing and delivering research relevant to sustainable fashion, consumption, behaviour change, communities, sustainability or climate action.
Experience of working with communities or external partners, building trust and adapting research methods to different participants and settings.
Ability to select appropriate qualitative and/or quantitative methods, analyse evidence and explain its limitations, with knowledge of research ethics and responsible data management.
Ability to plan and prioritise a focused research programme, meet agreed deadlines and communicate findings clearly to academic, practitioner and community audiences.
Additional Information
Salary Grade Ac2 - Starting from £23,736 rising to £26,611 per annum, pro rata £39,560 – £44,352

The salary range shows the potential maximum pay progression in addition to any annual inflationary increase to your pay. Please note that our default position is to appoint into the lower end of the range, unless there are exceptional circumstances.

This is a Part Time 0.6fte Fixed Term Contract for 1 Year in the first instance, with the opportunity to extend until 30th August 2030.

Interview Date - 16th December 2026

Special Conditions
The role requires regular in-person working at SOMER in Bath and with project partners and community hubs. UK travel and occasional evening or weekend work may be required.

 Due to the nature of this post regretfully we cannot accept applications that do not have the Right to Work/Live in the UK therefore your application will be rejected.

Staff Benefits

We offer a wide range of great benefits at BSU, including
Generous pension scheme (Local Government Pension Scheme/Teacher's Pension Scheme). This is a defined benefit pension scheme which pays members a secure income for life, post-retirement
Enhanced paid leave - 41 - 46 days depending on the role (Full Time) - more details here: https://apphub.bathspa.ac.uk/StaffBenefits
Family friendly policies including hybrid working, flexible work environment, on-site nursery, and a sector-leading enhanced maternity scheme 
Employee Assistance Programme which offers access to on-demand GP appointments, wellbeing support and advice, and access to counselling
Transport schemes including Electric Vehicle Scheme and Cycle to Work
Wide range of discounts and financial benefits, accessed through and easy-to-use app
For further details about all our staff benefits, have a look at our rewards page: https://www.bathspa.ac.uk/work-at-bath-spa/rewards-and-benefits/

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible.
About Bath Spa University
At Bath Spa University, we believe in the power of education to break down barriers to opportunity and to transform lives. We are the Professionally Creative for the future. Professional Creativity transcends subject disciplines, and is just as important for our sciences, education, business and law subjects as it is for our sector leading creative industries provision. We connect learners, staff and external partners with applied research and innovation. We power inclusive growth through skills development and practice based, innovation – intensive learning for all.

Our main Newton park campus is based in stunning countryside just a few minutes from a World Heritage City. We are also proud to offer courses to students at our other campuses around Bath, and in London at our Canary Wharf and Hackney sites.

An impressive 84% of our staff said they would recommend the University to a friend as a good place to work. 

We are a community of colleagues, striving for excellence to ensure students thrive. Our values are:
Respect 
Inclusivity 
Collaboration
Sustainability
We are committed to maintaining a safe and secure environment for our students, staff, and community. We foster inclusivity, celebrating and respecting differences. We welcome diversity and encourage applications from all backgrounds and genders. We consider our recruitment practices to be comprehensive and unbiased; ensuring fairness, transparency, and equal opportunity for all.

Information about visa sponsorship

Under the 2006 Immigration, Nationality and Asylum Act the University has a duty to prevent illegal working by carrying out document checks on all potential employees to confirm that a person has the right to work in the UK.

Please note that the University has a legal responsibility to ensure that all employees are entitled to live and work in the UK.

For some vacancies (those requiring specific specialist skills or in shortage occupations) we may be able to obtain a certificate of sponsorship for a suitably qualified applicant. Due to the limited availability of sponsorship resources, not all vacancies in this category will be eligible for Skilled Worker sponsorship. Sponsorship eligibility will be assessed on a role-by-role basis and is normally limited to positions that meet the University's workforce and immigration criteria.

In light of this, for most vacancies it will be unlikely that permission to work in the UK would be granted.

 You will plan, design & conduct socio-technical and human-factors research with security analysts, cybersecurity incident-response teams, healthcare and assisted-living personnel, and technology providers. Your research will inform user requirements and evaluate trust, usability and human decision-making within the project’s pilots. You will contribute to pilot monitoring, data collection and analysis, and the design of crisis simulation exercises examining communication and coordination during incidents. You will produce peer-reviewed publications, project deliverables and reports.

 The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic.

 The Department of Physics undertakes forefront research from fundamental particles to the furthest reaches of the universe, alongside training the next generation of leaders in physics. Join the Oxford ATLAS Group to lead searches for dark matter or triple-Higgs production and contribute to reconstruction and trigger performance at the LHC.

 About the Role 

 The ATLAS Group at the University of Oxford seeks two postdoctoral researchers to take leading roles in data analysis and reconstruction/trigger work on the ATLAS experiment. One post-holder will lead searches for triple-Higgs production, while the other will lead searches for dark matter in semi-invisible signatures.

 Both will contribute to missing transverse momentum reconstruction or jet reconstruction/tagging at offline or trigger level. You will manage your own research, analyse scientific data with novel techniques, develop or maintain software, and collaborate with colleagues across partner institutions. Responsibilities include supporting DPhil students; preparing scientific publications and presenting research at ATLAS meetings, workshops and conferences; and the opportunity to teach. Oxford has a large ATLAS group active in Standard Model, Higgs and beyond-Standard-Model analyses, detector upgrades, trigger and reconstruction, and ML/AI applications.

 These full-time, externally funded appointments run until 31 October 2030, with a possibility of renewal. Oxford is the preferred base, although CERN may be possible by agreement; hybrid working may be supported according to operational needs.

 About You 

 You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD/DPhil in experimental particle physics or a closely related field, with a proven track record of high-quality research and enthusiasm for the scientific goals of the post. You will be able to identify objectives, plan and execute research to deadlines, and programme confidently in C++ and Python.

 You will have excellent written and oral communication skills, including publishing and presenting research, and be self-motivated with the ability to guide graduate students. You will work collaboratively in a diverse team and demonstrate a commitment to inclusivity and diversity in physics. You must be willing to travel to CERN or other workshops and conferences as required, or to Oxford if based at CERN.

 It is desirable if candidates hold a PhD in collider physics and have experience in collider data analysis, including new-physics searches, searches involving semi-invisible detector signatures (one post), or multi-Higgs physics (one post). Experience with the reconstruction, tagging, or triggering of missing transverse momentum or hadronic jets is required, as is familiarity with the ROOT package, ATLAS software frameworks and expertise in advanced statistical methods. Candidates should also have experience in and an interest in designing and applying Machine Learning techniques. Experience in, or an interest in, science outreach and public engagement is also desirable.

 Application Process 

 You will be required to upload a CV, and a supporting statement explaining how you meet each selection criterion and your research interests, and provide details of two referees. Applicants should ask their two referees to send reference letters directly to:  julieta.estremadoyro-vermejo@physics.ox.ac.uk by the closing date. Please upload application documents as PDF files.

 Interviews are expected to take place during week commencing 25th January 2027; and will take place over Teams.

About the Role  

About the Role

The Research Assistant will support a research project led by Dr Sam Altmann in Econometrics, with a focus on empirical industrial organisation and structural econometrics.

The project investigates the empirical content of models of storable goods, such as laundry detergent, in the spirit of Hendel and Nevo’s 2006 paper in Econometrica. The research aims to understand what can be learned about the demand for these types of goods from just standard panel data on household purchases. 

A key component of the project is the replication of the estimator used in Hendel and Nevo 2006, as well as a simulation study to validate their estimator.

About You

The Research Assistant will play a central role in running a simulation study of Hendel and Nevo’s estimator. In collaboration with and under the supervision of Dr Altmann, this will involve coding up a version of their estimation method, as well as writing code to allow the simulation of data from their model.

The role predominantly involves the coding of dynamic demand models, as well as Generalised Method of Moments estimators. Prior experience of both aspects is not necessary, but some familiarity or experience of coding dynamic choice problems (such as Bellman or Policy Iteration) and/or experience of coding maximum likelihood or method of moments estimators (such as multinomial logit) is required.

The position requires a high level of attention to detail, experience of statistical programming, and the ability to follow and refine systematic coding procedures. The Research Assistant will also contribute to ensuring the reliability and reproducibility of the simultation study through careful documentation and validation.

About the School

The School of Economics and Finance is a leader in teaching and research at both the national and international level. It has a range of both undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including programmes that are jointly run with other Schools. The School has over 1000 undergraduate students, and over 500 postgraduate taught students. It offers excellent facilities and resources to enhance learning, including offering training and access to real time trading software to both UG and PGT students.    

About Queen Mary

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

Benefits

We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

 UCL, based in Bloomsbury, is a welcoming, inclusive university situated at the heart of one of the world’s greatest cities. UCL is a top-ranked university in the UK for research in psychology, psychiatry & neuroscience.

 DCAL is the leading research centre in the field of Deafness, Cognition and Language in Europe. It is a bilingual centre which brings together leading deaf and hearing researchers in the fields of linguistics, psychology and neuroscience. DCAL researchers study language – its origins, structure, use, development, processes and relationship with cognition, using the unique perspective of deafness and deaf communication.

 “SignGPT” is a 5-year project (2025-2030) which brings DCAL together with the Centre for Vision Speech and Signal Processing at the University of Surrey, and the Visual Geometry Group at the University of Oxford. The project, funded by the UK Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), aims to leverage annotated sign language data from the British Sign Language (BSL) Corpus ( http://www.bslcorpusproject.org ) and other sources to build tools to allow spoken language to be automatically translated into photo-realistic sign language and video of sign language to be translated into spoken language.

 About the role 

 This is an exciting opportunity to work with the UCL/DCAL component of “SignGPT” – a research team led by Prof Kearsy Cormier and Prof Bencie Woll. The team works closely with other collaborators on the project – Lead PI Prof Richard Bowden (University of Surrey) and Prof Andrew Zisserman (University of Oxford) and their teams.

 The postholder will provide linguistic expertise to the design of AI tools and assets and will then use these tools to conduct linguistic research. They will also help organise the user community workshops, post news items online, and contribute to writing up of the project findings along with the PI/CIs. The post holder will receive training, support and mentoring as appropriate to the role. The post-holder will be based at the UCL Deafness, Cognition and Language Research Centre (DCAL).

 The position is offered for 36 months.

 Appointment at Grade 7 is dependent upon having been awarded a PhD; if this is not the case, initial appointment will be at Grade 6B (salary £40,603 - £43,749 per annum) with payment at Grade 7 being backdated to the date of final submission of the PhD Thesis. To be considered eligible for this post, applicants must have formally submitted their PhD thesis and must either have successfully completed their viva examination or have an agreed viva date scheduled within 3 months of the post’s commencement date.

 About you 

 You will hold a doctoral degree in linguistics or related area (e.g. applied linguistics, corpus/computational linguistics, psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, data science) or evidence of substantial relevant research experience in one or more of these areas. You will also have fluent skills in British Sign Language (BSL) or another sign language. You will be based at UCL DCAL and will work closely with other project members at DCAL. You will also liaise regularly with researchers at Surrey and Oxford who will be doing the main technical work.

 DCAL particularly encourages applications from deaf and deafblind people for all posts.

 Further details

 Background of department/role 

 We are seeking an experienced, highly motivated, and analytically strong researcher to join a multi‑disciplinary team on a Home Office‑funded project addressing domestic abuse and stalking perpetrator behaviour.

 The project will generate a robust evidence base on the effectiveness of multi‑agency responses, examining how coordinated interventions shape perpetrator attitudes and behaviour and how victims and survivors (including children) can be more effectively supported and safeguarded.

 Working closely with the Principal Investigator and the research team, the post‑holder will lead key elements of a rigorous mixed‑methods evaluation, confidently handling complex, large‑scale quantitative datasets drawn from multiple agencies (e.g., administrative, service‑level, and outcomes data), applying advanced analytical techniques to assess intervention effectiveness and engagement patterns across diverse cohorts, and ensuring data quality, transparency, and methodological integrity throughout.

 Alongside this, they will conduct trauma‑informed qualitative research, designing and delivering ethically sensitive interviews with practitioners, stakeholders, and where appropriate, service users, demonstrating sound judgement around consent, participant wellbeing, safeguarding, and the particular ethical and emotional considerations inherent in research on domestic abuse and stalking.

 The successful candidate will integrate quantitative and qualitative strands into a coherent evaluation framework, triangulating evidence to illuminate how multi‑agency collaborations operate in practice, where they achieve impact, and where system improvements are required.

 A strong track record in academic writing is essential. The role includes leading and contributing to peer‑reviewed publications, policy‑relevant research reports, and concise evidence briefings tailored to academic, practitioner, and government audiences, as well as presenting findings at conferences and stakeholder events.

 Candidates will bring substantive research experience and practical/working knowledge of domestic abuse and stalking, proven expertise in analysing large, complex datasets using appropriate statistical software, and a demonstrable commitment to trauma‑informed, ethically robust practice.

 Experience evaluating complex interventions or multi‑agency programmes and familiarity with commissioned or government evaluation standards are advantageous, as is the ability to communicate complex findings with clarity to non‑specialist audiences and to work effectively across disciplines and sectors.

Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Social Science

Job id: 163365. Salary: £45,829 - £53,462 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance.

About us

The British Election Study is the longest-running and most authoritative survey of electoral behaviour in the UK, tracking the attitudes and behaviour of British voters at every general election since 1964.

Royal Holloway with King's College London and the University of Manchester have been awarded £4.9million by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) to lead the British Election Study (BES) for the next five years (2027-2032). During this period, the team will introduce new methods, new data and new ways of making the BES accessible to researchers, policymakers, journalists and the public.

Within the BES project, the Department of Informatics at King’s College London is responsible for developing the BES’s Artificial Intelligence Interface (the BES-AII). Integrated into the BES website (https://www.britishelectionstudy.com/), the BES-AII will offer users the opportunity to access and interact with BES data through natural language queries, making the BES data more accessible to non-specialist users than ever before.

About the role

The Department of Informatics at King’s College London is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Researcher to support the British Election Study (BES; 60% FTE) and to carry out independent research in computational social science (40% FTE) of relevance to the BES and/or broader research on political attitudes.

For the BES parts of the role, the researcher will lead the development of data exploration and visualisation tools to be integrated into the BES’s AI Interface (BES-AII; a system which will allow users to explore and export BES data using natural language queries). The researcher will collaborate with the BES-AII lead developer to ensure tools are appropriately integrated into the public facing website.

The researcher will collaborate with the BES team (mainly political scientists) to identify tools of broad use across diverse BES stakeholder groups (academics, policy makers, the public, etc.). This includes the “Voting Insights for Better Engagement” tool which will let end users compare their political attitudes to the attitudes of BES survey participants (for a similar tool, see https://votecompass.uk/ ). The researcher will also play a small role in supporting the integration of a human-AI collaboration tool into the BES survey which uses large language models to help collect rich, but narrowly scoped qualitative data from BES survey participants, at scale. 

Throughout the project, the researcher will contribute to outreach activities, will support extensive (AI) safety testing, and will contribute to ensuring that the BES maintains its duty to remain politically impartial.

The remaining 40% of the researcher's time can be used to pursue an independent research project developed with supervisor Dr Falkenberg (and other members of the BES team) related to computational social science and of relevance to the BES and/or broader public opinion research. We note that a candidate's suitability for the BES data exploration and visualisation parts of the project will be prioritised over their suitability for the independent research role.

The researcher will be based in the Department of Informatics and will report to Dr Max Falkenberg (primary supervisor), and Professor Rosie Campbell (second supervisor; political science lead for the BES at KCL).

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 24 months starting on 1st April 2027.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

1.      A PhD in a relevant subject (completed, or near completion).

2.      A track record of high-quality interdisciplinary research and engagement (proven through a record of publications) and willingness to actively work with and communicate clearly to individuals with diverse backgrounds (academics, policy makers, the public, etc.).

3.      Proven data exploration and/or data visualisation skills.

4.      An independent research vision related to computational social science.

5.      A full commitment to maintaining ethical research practices, including in relation to the use of AI, and when working with sensitive political data.

6.      Excellent communication, both written and verbal skills.

7.      Excellent organizational and teamworking skills.

8.      Enthusiasm to work at the boundary of computer science and politics.

Desirable criteria

1.       Experience leading public-facing outreach activities.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

Please submit an additional statement outlining your research proposal, maximum 1 page A4 including references.

About the Role

This role is an exciting opportunity to join the operational team of a diverse, global network that serves more than 220 doctoral and postdoctoral researchers working on open education and related topics as well as a wider community of practice. The Global Open Graduate Network (GO-GN) (https://go-gn.net) was founded in 2012 and has been managed by the award-winning team at The Open University (UK) in the Institute of Educational Technology (IET) since 2015.

GO-GN plays a critical role in the open education community, providing extra-institutional, informal support to doctoral researchers in more than 30 different countries around the world. We support open education researchers by raising the profile of research in this area, facilitating activities across the network, developing openness as a process of research and promoting diversity, equity and inclusion in open education research and practice. We achieve our aims through various activities including face-to-face workshops aligned with major open education conferences, scholarships, online events and collaborative activities including the co-creation of openly licensed outputs and collaboration with other stakeholders in the open education space. GO-GN is a high impact network with ca. 80,000 citations of doctoral researcher and alumni member research as of October 2026.

The GO-GN coordination team currently comprises of three academics with support from professional services. The team utilise open and agile approaches in a fast-paced and member led environment. The Research Associate will play a key role in the GO-GN team, at an exciting time in the network’s development. Our current focus is sustainability pathways for the network, which include building on our exploration of federation through pilot hubs, evidencing the network’s impact and a communications refresh. Other activities for this phase include collaborative research projects, further openly licensed guides and an enhanced funding scheme for members.

Key Responsibilities
Attend weekly GO-GN meetings (face-to-face/online).
Craft appropriate social media and newsletter content for the GO-GN audience.
Co-organise and host GO-GN webinars with external speakers.
Co-produce reports and high-quality, open licensed publications in collaboration with project leads and the wider GO-GN community.
Contribute to organising, running and documenting GO-GN workshops.
Participation and presentation at external events such as conferences, as required.
Contribute to GO-GN sustainability planning, as required.
Strong time management and project-planning skills.
Observe the principles of equality, diversity, and inclusion.
To undertake other duties as may be reasonably requested and that are commensurate with the nature and grade of the post.

PhD in Educational Technology, Technology-Enhanced Learning, or another relevant field.
Knowledge of open educational resources, open research practices or similar.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Experience of Participating in research of international quality.
Experience in research design.
Ability to collect and analyse qualitative and quantitive data including interviews, focus groups, observations, online surveys and statistical analysis.
Experience of working with social media platforms, building online communities and crafting content for academic audiences.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team, ideally in interdisciplinary teams.
Experience of authoring, co-authoring or editing academic outputs including  journal articles, books, research report.
Ability to visit IET at least once a month for a face-to-face meeting with the team.

About the Role  

About the Role

In this project we are looking into the mechanisms that lead to production of autoantibodies in inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.  We will be using Behçet’s disease and rheumatoid arthritis as disease models to investigate the interactions between B cells and Gamma Delta T cells. 

Key duties involve:

Processing of patients’ blood samples; isolation of purified population of gamma delta T cells and B cells for co-culturing and RNA isolation; performing flow cytometry and biochemical experiments; conducting bioinformatics analyses.

About You

Qualifications in molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics or a related area. Desired good knowledge of immunology and experience in cell culture, cell sorting and flow cytometry techniques. 

About the School/Department/Institute/Project

The Institute of Dentistry is part of the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry at Queen Mary University of London (QMUL), a leading Russell Group university. It integrates research and teaching, combining a heritage dating back to 1911 and roots from St Bartholomew's and The London Hospital Medical College, with modern scientific inquiry. Our centre is located in The Blizard Institute, Whitechapel campus. Our research group investigates the phenotypic and functional characteristics of innate and adaptive immune cells in oral diseases and systemic inflammatory diseases with oral manifestations. The specific project aims to understand the interactions between gamma delta T cell and B cells in Behçet’s disease leading to autoantibody production. For this we use approaches including cell and molecular biology, in vitro cell functional assays, flow cytometry, immunological techniques and bioinformatics.

Job Title: Research Fellow in Biophysics of Morphogenesis

Reference:  597

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 27 February 2032

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Monday 14 December 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                       

Full time Salary Range: £36,320.00 - £46,970.00 per annum

About the Role

Applications are invited for a Research Fellow position in the Saunders lab to work on a BBSRC funded project titled: "From Genes to Form: Deciphering Molecular and Mechanical Interplay During Tissue Morphogenesis". This multi-team project, comprising labs at the Francis Crick Institute (Briscoe), UCL (Charras, Molodtsov), Edinburgh (Lowell) and Warwick (Saunders) will unravel how complex form emerges during development utilising a novel organoid system combined with biophysical perturbation and theory.

 
Understanding how genetic information encodes tissue architecture represents one of biology's grand challenges. Tissue shape emerges from feedback between gene expression, cell-generated forces, spatial constraints, and intercellular signalling. Our team will reveal fundamental principles linking genome to shape by analysing how gene regulation, signalling networks, mechanical forces, and tissue geometry integrate through multiscale feedback to generate reproducible architecture. Our aim is a predictive understanding through sustained integration of experimental embryology, precision mechanical measurements, synthetic control, and computational modelling. The position will be principally based in the Saunders lab at Warwick. We will predominantly utilise live imaging and biophysical measurements of organoid systems. This work will be integrated with genetic studies and theoretical models to deepen our understanding of how complex form emerges in development.

 
Please note this is an on-campus based role due to the nature of the work, therefore we cannot accommodate any work from home.  Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to Professor Timothy Saunders Timothy.Saunders@warwick.ac.uk

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with expertise in experimental biophysics and/or organoid systems. We also welcome applications from people with expertise in quantitative biology and imaging backgrounds. Applicants should be proficient in cell culture and light microscopy. You must have a high degree of independence so that you can carry out research tasks and realise outputs (including publications). 

 

If you have not yet been awarded your PhD but are near submission or have recently submitted your PhD, any offers of employment will be made as Research Assistant at the top of level 5 within the University grade structure. Upon successful award of your PhD and evidence of this fact, you will be promoted to Research Fellow on the first point of the level 6 of the University grade structure, unless exceptional experience applies to warrant a higher salary.

About the Department

Warwick Medical School is one of the UK's leading medical schools, with a reputation for excellence in research and teaching.

 

WMS has a diverse portfolio of undergraduate, postgraduate and research education, alongside continuing professional development across the healthcare sector. This role provides an opportunity to contribute directly to the development of our education provision and other priority projects across the School. 

 

We employ high calibre people in many fields, including academics, teaching and research staff, administrative staff, and professional support staff. We welcome staff and students from all of the world with diverse backgrounds and experience. One of our key teaching strengths is the number of academics we have still working in their chosen clinical speciality alongside their teaching commitments. This ensures that they bring up to date knowledge and experience as well as first rate teaching experience. Our research is excellent due to the calibre of our researchers working across the fields of biomedical sciences, health sciences and clinical trials. The university's rich research environment and our regional, national and international partnerships enable us to carry out ground breaking, impactful work.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed. 

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.
